14 killed, 28 injured as truck hits devotees near temple in Madhya Pradesh's Gwalior
sources.content: In a horrific accident in Madhya Pradesh's Gwalior, 13 people were killed and 28 others were injured after a truck rammed into devotees and shops when they were waiting near a temple.  The incident happened at around 1:30 am on the Sheetlamata Mandir road when the truck driver lost control and the vehicle hit devotees before coming to a halt by smashing into the temple wall, which led to a collapse. Kolkata Durga Puja stampede: Police detain 12, including organisersAn investigator said the truck’s brakes may have failed, forcing the driver to swerve left in a desperate attempt to control the vehicle. Had it continued straight, he said, it would have ploughed into at least 600 to 700 devotees.The truck driver fled from the spot, and police teams were searching for him.The accident has raised concerns about security arrangements at the shrine, as the truck, with a Punjab registration number, entered the no-entry zone, officials told PTI.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed grief over the loss of lives and announced ex gratia relief of Rs 2 lakh to the next of kin of each deceased and Rs 50,000 for each injured.“Distressed to learn about the loss of lives due to a mishap in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. My condolences to the bereaved families. Praying for the speedy recovery of the injured,” Modi said in an X post.Rescue operations are underway under the supervision of senior officials.

stories.primary_headline: EC-SIR row | Congress says nothing can save Gyanesh Kumar, seeks major revamp of the poll body

primary_source.headline: EC-SIR row | Congress says nothing can save Gyanesh Kumar, seeks major revamp of the poll body
primary_source.content:
New Delhi: As the Election Commission "resumes" distribution of "readable" electoral rolls to parties after a "gap of eight years", Congress on Sunday said "nothing can save" Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar while insisting that a "thorough" revamp of the poll body and its IT system is required.General Secretary (Communications) Jairam Ramesh said the decision to provide electoral rolls in readable PDF format  was the result of the whole nation being on the streets against the "vote chors".EC-SIR row | People's Movement march seeking Gyanesh Kumar's removal on October 23The attack comes as the Congress prepares to host I.N.D.I.A. bloc parties at a rally in Ramlila Maidan on November 1 against the CEC.In a post on 'X', he said over the past two years, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and the Congress have been "persistent, insistent and consistent" in demanding that the EC provide electoral rolls in searchable format to all parties. पिछले दो वर्षों से लोकसभा में विपक्ष के नेता श्री राहुल गांधी और कांग्रेस पार्टी लगातार, मजबूती से और पुरजोर तरीके से यह मांग करते आ रहे हैं कि भारत निर्वाचन आयोग सभी राजनीतिक दलों को मतदाता सूची ऐसे डिजिटल फॉर्मेट में उपलब्ध कराए, जिसमें मतदाताओं के नाम और अन्य जानकारी आसानी से…&mdash; Jairam Ramesh (@Jairam_Ramesh) October 18, 2026
 

"The demand was repeatedly refused by the ECI - which stopped providing searchable voter rolls in 2018 when the Congress found lakhs of bogus voters in Madhya Pradesh. The demand was denied for eight years to enable 'vote chori'," he claimed.Referring to the October 15 announcement by the EC on providing voter lists in readable format, he said "every time Vote Chori is caught, the Modi government adopts a new tactic: stopping readable voter rolls, fake voter additions, SIR. But not this time.""Nothing can save the CEC Gyanesh Kumar who, acting on the instructions of the PM and the HM, has destroyed public trust and confidence in the ECI. He simply has to go. But that alone will not be enough. The ECI itself along with its IT system has to be thoroughly revamped," he said. TThe SIR, that has put the Constitutional right to vote for over 13 crore Indians at risk, has to be suspended forthwith, he added.

sources.headline: EC-SIR row | People's Movement march seeking Gyanesh Kumar's removal on October 23
sources.content: New Delhi: The 'People Against SIR', a coalition of various organisations, on Sunday announced a ‘People’s March to Reclaim Democracy’ on October 23 across India demanding removal and prosecution of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, scrapping of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and restoration of voters whose names have been deleted.With the slogan ‘Har Haath Mein Tiranga, Har Gali Jantar Mantar’ (In Every Hand Tricolor, Every Street is Jantar Mantar), the coalition of civil society organisations, farmer unions, trade unions, students and youth organisations, academicians, artistes and activists said the protest marches with tricolor in their hands will be held at tehsil, district, state and national level.Nothing can save CEC; SIR must be suspended forthwith: CongressThe coalition, which included actor-activist Prakash Raj, Kisan Sabha leader P Krishnaprasad and CPI(ML)L leader N Sai Balaji, said the ‘People's March’ will not request police permission anywhere while "strictly warning" police, paramilitary and prisons against using the "brute state force" against peaceful protesters.&nbsp;If the march is blocked by police, it said, the protesters will peacefully hold the People's Parliament and disperse later after singing the national anthem.Claiming that the CEC helped the BJP to remain in power, it recalled that the Supreme Court has maintained that it did not upheld alteration of Form 6 used for inclusion of new voters.&nbsp;“Gyanesh Kumar has violated his Constitutional pledge and must be prosecuted. But the Prime Minister himself is protecting the criminal...Without Parliament impeaching CEC Gyanesh Kumar, the Prime Minister cannot come out of the full-blown constitutional standoff,” it said.Calling upon farmers, workers, daily wage earners, traders, entrepreneurs, journalists, advocates, teachers, employees, artists, intellectuals, women, youth, students, adivasis, dalits and minorities to join the march, a statement said its demands include comprehensive electoral reforms, proportional representation, curb money/muscle power and legalise state funding of polls.The statement alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah have misused the Election Commission and erased the voting rights of 13.41 crore citizens through SIR.

stories.primary_headline: Durga Puja pandal stampede gives Mamata's TMC a ‘bhaipo’ in BJP to target

primary_source.headline: Durga Puja pandal stampede gives Mamata's TMC a ‘bhaipo’ in BJP to target
primary_source.content: Kolkata: The stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata has triggered a war of words in West Bengal politics, as the alleged association of two ruling Bharatiya Janata Party leaders and Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari’s nephew with the organisers provided fresh ammunition to the Mamata Banerjee faction of the Trinamool Congress to attack the government.Suvendu, himself, on October 12, inaugurated the Chorebagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samity’s pandal, where a stampede left 19 people dead and more than 20 injured on Sunday. The narrow entry and exit alleyways, limited space and inadequate crowd-control measures, deliberately dim lighting to match the pandal's theme, a sudden influx of visitors seeking shelter from the evening rain, and alleged lapses in police arrangements are blamed for the disaster.With Suvendu’s nephew, Debdeep Adhikari, being the chief patron of the organising committee, the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress, the TMC faction led by Mamata Banerjee, finally found a ‘bhaipo’ in the ruling BJP to train the guns on.&nbsp;“Guess who is closely associated with the Chorebagan Puja Pandal? CM Suvendu Adhikari’s BHAIPO,” the MAITC posted on X soon after the disaster. “When are you going to put your criminal nephew behind bars, Suvendu Babu?” posted Abhishek Banerjee, who has been at the receiving end of the ‘bhaipo (nephew)’ taunt ever since his ‘pisi (aunt)’, Mamata Banerjee, inducted him into the party she founded.The tragedy raised questions about whether the organisers had made adequate safety arrangements for the large crowds expected at the pandal. Its narrow entry and exit passageways, sloping route through the structure, and deliberately dim lighting intended to complement its theme may have heightened the risk of overcrowding and slowed visitor movement. The sudden influx of people seeking shelter from the evening rain further compounded the danger, while questions were raised about the police's preparedness to regulate the crowds and respond to the emergency.Not only Debdeep, but two other BJP leaders were also associated with this year’s Durga Puja of the Chorebagan Sarbojanin Durgotsav Samity, legislator Vijay Ojha as chairman and the saffron party’s North Kolkata district unit president, Tamoghna Ghosh, as chief adviser.The six people arrested by police after the incident include the secretary Raj Kumar Sewda and the vice president of the organising committee Santanu Dubey, but none are linked to the BJP.“The CM himself inaugurated Chorebagan Puja Pandal. Did he not look into security arrangements when he visited the pandal? Won’t he be held accountable for every single life lost?” the Mamata faction of the TMC asked, questioning whether the police would take any action against Debdeep, Vijay and Tamoghna.Soon after the stampede on Saturday, Suvendu and Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee rushed to Kolkata Medical College and Hospital, where the injured and deceased were initially taken. The chief minister visited the stampede site in the pre-dawn hours of Sunday.“Attempts are being made by some people to reap political dividends from such a tragedy. They will not succeed. The families of the deceased and injured told me that they had full faith in the state government and me,” Suvendu said on Sunday. He added that a probe was underway and the government would not spare anyone found responsible for the disaster. “No one should indulge in politics over death,” he said.&nbsp;Kolkata stampede | 'CM himself inaugurated Chorebagan puja pandal, will he be held accountable?': Mamata AITC attacks Suvendu govtHe sought to turn the tables on his predecessor, Mamata Banerjee, and the TMC government she had headed.&nbsp;The chief minister cited several tragedies during the TMC’s tenure, including the collapse of an under-construction flyover in north Kolkata in 2016, which killed seven people, and the collapse of Majherhat Bridge in 2018, which killed three. He also referred to the Panihati festival incident in July 2022, in which three people died; the electrocution deaths of nine people during waterlogging in Kolkata after heavy rain ahead of Durga Puja in 2025; and flash floods in North Bengal that year, which killed around 100 people.“What was the then chief minister doing?” Suvendu questioned, hitting back at Mamata.&nbsp;“This is not the time to indulge in a political blame game,” Samik Bhattacharya, the state BJP chief, said, responding to the Opposition's criticism. &nbsp;&nbsp;The Opposition, however, is not ready to relent. “Where were the police when the incident took place? There was no response even after calls were made to the police control room,” Subhankar Sarkar, president of the West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee, said.What further sharpened criticism of the city police and the state government is that, over the past few days, cops in several places were seen evicting or trying to evict bookstalls set up by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) near the Durga Puja pandals. Mohammed Salim, the state secretary of the CPI(M), questioned the priorities of the police, stating that the residents living near the pandal of the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja Samity complained about a lack of police to manage the crowd as well as the unavailability of an adequate number of ambulances to take the injured to hospital after the disaster.&nbsp;As in several other Durga Puja organising clubs across West Bengal, the leadership of the Chorebagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samity changed after the TMC’s defeat in the Assembly elections earlier this year and the BJP’s rise to power. Jayanta Bandopadhyay, who was known to be associated with the TMC, was removed from the puja committee’s leadership, although he had managed the festival for several years. Jayanta had also performed the Khunti Puja, the ceremony marking the start of pandal construction, before he and others were sidelined and a new committee comprising people linked to the ruling BJP was formed. The new committee subsequently performed a second Khunti Puja in the presence of several BJP leaders.

primary_source.headline: Gwalior temple tragedy: MP CM orders removal of SP, suspension of 8 other police personnel
primary_source.content: Bhopal: Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav on Sunday ordered the removal of the Gwalior City Superintendent of Police and the suspension of eight other personnel after the temple accident that claimed 14 lives when a truck ploughed into devotees.The speeding truck ran over several devotees outside the Sheetla Mata temple in Gwalior district early Sunday and then rammed into its entrance gate, killing 14 persons and injuring 28 others, including two police personnel, officials said. Seven of those injured were in critical condition.A wall of the temple crashed under the impact of the collision, they said.'Came like a storm': Eyewitnesses recall truck's deadly dash towards Gwalior templeThe incident, which occurred around 1.30 am outside the temple near a slope on Chinor Road, raised concerns about security arrangements at the shrine, as the truck, with a Punjab registration number, entered the no-entry zone, officials said."The accident occurred because the truck entered a prohibited area," Yadav told reporters in Indore.The chief minister said he had directed the district administration to conduct a fact-based inquiry and submit a report.Later, in a post on X, Yadav said his government has ordered the removal of the Gwalior CSP from his post and the suspension of three station house officers, a traffic inspector, a head constable and three constables.A detailed inquiry has been ordered to fix responsibility and ensure strict action against those found guilty, he said."The safety of all citizens is paramount. To prevent the recurrence of such incidents in future, security arrangements will be reviewed and necessary steps taken. No negligence will be tolerated at any level in public safety," he said.Yadav also announced compensation of Rs 4 lakh each for the kin of the deceased and said the government would bear the treatment expenses of those seriously injured in the accident. The persons who suffered minor injuries would receive financial assistance of Rs 50,000 each, he added.The impact brought down a temple wall, trapping people under the debris.The bodies and injured persons were shifted to different hospitals, including Gwalior's trauma centre.Relatives of victims gathered near the post-mortem facility at the trauma centre and expressed anger over the incident, with many questioning how a heavy truck could enter an area where, they claimed, even a bicycle could not pass.Lokendra Singh Tomar, nephew of the deceased Sarla Tomar, asked how the truck was allowed to enter the temple premises despite security arrangements.14 killed, 28 injured as truck hits devotees near temple in Madhya Pradesh's Gwalior His aunt was on her way to offer prayers at the shrine, he told reporters and demanded answers from those responsible for the accident.Pawan Rathore (23), a resident of Gadaipur in Gwalior’s Hazira area, was among those killed. His family took the body away amid inconsolable grief. He had gone to the temple to offer prayers when the accident occurred.Sandeep, a relative of injured devotee Nikesh, said the family received a phone call around 5 am informing them that Nikesh had been hurt at the temple. When they reached the hospital, he was in critical condition with both legs fractured and was placed on a ventilator, he added.

stories.primary_headline: Five killed after car, trying to escape pothole, crashes into state transport bus in Maharashtra's Beed

primary_source.headline: Five killed after car, trying to escape pothole, crashes into state transport bus in Maharashtra's Beed
primary_source.content: Beed: Five people, among them an 11-year-old boy, were killed after their car swerved to avoid potholes and collided with a state transport bus in Maharashtra's Beed district on Sunday morning, police said.The accident occurred around 11 am at Shindewadi Cross Road on the Khamgaon-Pandharpur National Highway in Majalgaon tehsil, around 55 km from the district headquarters, an official said.He said that the victims, all residents of Majalgaon, were travelling towards Tuljapur in neighbouring Dharashiv district when their car crashed into a Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) bus coming from the opposite direction.The collision reduced the car to a mangled heap of metal, killing all five occupants on the spot, the official said.According to the police, the deceased have been identified as Omkar Mahadev Giri (24), Gajanan Mahadev Namdas (38), his son Samarth (11), Somnath Bade (23), and Anil Acharya (40).Speeding car crash triggers communal, moral and political row in KeralamCCTV footage from the area showed the speeding car lose control while attempting to avoid potholes on a bridge, leading to the head-on crash with the bus, the official said.The fatal crash triggered public anger over the deteriorating condition of roads on the Majalgaon-Telgaon stretch. Locals staged a road blockade alleging that substandard construction and poor maintenance had left fissures and uneven surfaces across the highway, turning the arterial road into an accident zone.Traffic came to a standstill for several hours on the highway due to the protest before senior police and district officials arrived at the scene, pacified the protesters, and restored traffic flow.

Locals staged a road blockade alleging that substandard construction and poor maintenance had left fissures and uneven surfaces across the highway, turning the arterial road into an accident zone.Traffic came to a standstill for several hours on the highway due to the protest before senior police and district officials arrived at the scene, pacified the protesters, and restored traffic flow.
